title: Robichaux's band at Lincoln Park and the balloonist
summary: As a school boy he heard Robichaux at Lincoln Park on Sundays, with a balloonist parachuting for excitement.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you hear the John Robichaud band yourself? Huh? Did you hear that band, the John Robichaud band?

Oh, certainly. When I was a young fellow going to school, I was in short pants. But I'd put on long pants, my brother's long pants, and I'd go to a place where John Robichaud played regular. He was the famous band of the town. They'd play a place they'd call up in Calderon, they'd call it the Lincoln's Pop. He's the only band mostly had played there. And his band was... Did you say in the open air?
Huh? In the open air?

Well, I tell you, they had a dance hall, and the dance was start at four o'clock in the evening, on Sunday evenings, in the yard. They danced in the yard. And they had a fellow, they called Buddy Bodley. He would go up in the balloons. And that's the largest place that place was packed.
A lot of trees and...
No, never had no trees. Just a big open place. Big open place, just like the ballpark.
He'd go up in a balloon, you say?
Every Sunday evening.
You mean to advertise his thing?
Well, it was excitement. They'd pay him, you know, for excitement like that. And the people would go out there.
Did he come down again?
I hope so. He went up the balloon several times, and the last time he opened the balloon, they come down on the wire. He fell on the electrolyte wire.
What kind of balloon? Is it filled with hot air or something?
Yeah. Probably shoot something, go up and come down. What happened when he hit the wire?
Did he execute it or did he die?
No, he hit the wire, but he come right on down. Man, that guy was like a monkey. Come down the post. Oh, yeah?
How would he come down? He looked, he was down by the post.

It looked like he married that thing to get the electrolyte post. When he hit that post, he got up, come on down. Man, the people just clapped for that. How did he get, when he went up the balloon, how would he come back down?
Parachute? Yeah.
That was big excitement.
That would be in late afternoon.
